long_biography.plain_text:
Kerimov built his fortune by treating companies as investments rather than operating platforms. Trained as an economist in Dagestan, he advanced from a factory role into finance and acquired control of Nafta Moskva. He reworked the former oil trader into a holding company, then profited from stakes in Gazprom, Sberbank and Polymetal before moving heavily into global banks.

The financial crisis exposed the risk of that concentrated strategy and cost him billions. A subsequent purchase in Polyus restored his position and shifted the family's economic centre towards gold. He transferred shares to his son, and formal ownership subsequently moved among other holders, separating the original investor from the asset's public title.
